coverage: Tuesday 11 Aug complete — Asia and US closes both final. Four parallel finders plus an adversarial verification pass that reconciled every percent change against Monday's published closes. US July CPI (20:30 SGT tonight) and Tencent's interim results (after the HK close today) both land AFTER this was written and are NOT in here.
tldr: THE DAY'S REAL SIGNAL IS A SHAPE, NOT A LEVEL: gold spiked to a two-month high of $4,432.74 in Asian hours and closed DOWN at ~$4,368 (-0.5%); silver touched a seven-week high near $66 and closed ~$64.71 (-1.5%). A failed breakout on a day when oil settled UP and the long end sits at 2007 highs is a different message from a quiet drift lower — the backdrop was supportive and the metals could not use it.

Your largest risk took its first down day of the week. At 1.6x IBKR margin a -1.5% spot silver move is roughly -2.4% on the position, and the intraday round trip from ~$66.30 to $64.71 is the kind of range that moves maintenance margin even when the close looks orderly. Check headroom BEFORE 20:30 SGT, not after.

SINGAPORE ANSWERED THE QUESTION — AND NOT THE WAY WE FEARED. The STI reopened after National Day and RALLIED 0.98% to 5,754.17 despite the 30Y at 5.254%, with MTI upgrading 2026 GDP to 4.5-5.5% from 2.0-4.0% and OCBC closing at a record (+3.5% to +3.8% depending on feed; DBS +0.86%). Every SGX change spans Friday-to-Tuesday, so it embeds three days of offshore news.

BUT YOUR REIT SLEEVE DIDN'T MARK AT ALL: Mapletree Logistics, Mapletree Industrial, MPACT and Keppel REIT each printed EXACTLY 0.00% — while on the same table CICT rose 2.03%, Frasers Centrepoint 0.90% and Keppel DC 0.45%. So it is NOT a REIT-wide rates story; it is specific to the names you hold. Single-source and worth checking against your broker marks today.

HK tech was the day's only real weakness: Hang Seng -1.10%, HS Tech -1.9%, Xiaomi -3.5% to HK$26.66 (about -HK$25,600 on your 26,662 units, and worse than the tech index itself), Tencent -2.2% to HK$470.80 into today's results, SMIC -1.36% closing near its low. Korea rose 0.73% and Japan was shut, so Asia split rather than moving as a bloc.

Oil did the opposite of fading — Brent SETTLED $88.91 (+1.4%), WTI $83.20 (+1.3%), a fifth straight gain to one-week highs, on doubt a US-Iran deal restores flows quickly. Correction to our own record: the $87.85/$82.30 we published for Monday were spot/CFD quotes, not exchange settlements; the true Monday settles were $87.72/$82.13.

THE FED PATH HARDENED AT THE MARGIN. Hammack — a 2026 voter who already dissented FOR a hike in July — says multiple increases will likely be needed and that 3.50-3.75% is not meaningfully restrictive. September is priced roughly 50/50 hike-versus-hold, down from 67% hike odds a week ago. There is no cut anywhere in that distribution.

Against that, the actual price-setting data is cooling: NFIB July showed net 31% raising selling prices (-7pts), net 28% planning increases (-4pts), and only 14% citing inflation as their top problem (-7pts, the first decline this year). Two-sided into tonight.

DATA-INTEGRITY: Japan was CLOSED Tuesday for Mountain Day, so no Nikkei close exists — if any app shows you one, it is Monday's 66,970.22 re-dated. Also rejected today: a 'fell 206 points' Hang Seng figure (the real delta is 284.67), a 3-year auction snippet conflated with a 2024 auction, a delayed 14:20 ET GDX quote served as the close, and syndicated 'gold gains a third session' headlines written off 02:17 GMT data.

regime.label: Metals rejected at the highs; everything defers to tonight's CPI
regime.oneLiner: Gold and silver both made multi-week highs and closed lower on a supportive backdrop, a voting Fed member argued for multiple hikes, and the September distribution now contains no cut at all.

topNews.headline: Gold hits a two-month high of $4,432.74 and closes DOWN at ~$4,368; silver hits a seven-week high near $66 and closes ~$64.71 (-1.5%)
topNews.actionable: Both reconcile exactly to Monday's published closes, so the moves are clean. The failed-breakout shape is the information: a supportive backdrop that the metals could not convert. Everything resets on CPI at 20:30 SGT, and the 1.6x levered silver is the position that behaves worst on a hot print.

topNews.headline: STI reopens and RALLIES +0.98% to 5,754.17 as MTI upgrades 2026 GDP to 4.5-5.5%; OCBC closes at a record
topNews.actionable: The feared long-end repricing of Singapore did not show up on day one, and an AI-capex-led growth year favours the banks over the REITs. OCBC at a record on a 22% profit beat now two sessions old is the concrete trim-or-hold decision.

topNews.headline: Your Mapletree and Keppel REIT names printed EXACTLY 0.00% while CICT +2.03%, FCT +0.90% and Keppel DC +0.45% moved
topNews.actionable: Not a sector rates story — three peer REITs traded on the same table. Verify against your broker marks today; this is the one item in the brief that does not meet the verification standard of the rest.

topNews.headline: HK tech leads the drag: HS Tech -1.9%, Xiaomi -3.5% to HK$26.66, Tencent -2.2% into today's results, SMIC -1.36%
topNews.actionable: HS Tech's -1.9% is the relevant benchmark for your book, not the -1.10% headline. Xiaomi underperformed even the tech index, so this was stock-specific weakness on top of sector weakness — roughly -HK$25,600 on your position.

topNews.headline: Hammack says multiple hikes may be needed; September priced ~50/50 hike-versus-hold, from 67% hike odds a week ago
topNews.actionable: A voting member who already dissented for a hike is arguing for a sequence, and no cut appears anywhere in the September distribution. Rising real-rate expectations are the textbook headwind for levered non-yielding metals.

topNews.headline: Brent settles $88.91 (+1.4%), WTI $83.20 — fifth straight gain — while Qatar says Oman-Iran Hormuz talks are at an 'advanced stage'
topNews.actionable: Crude settling at one-week highs on the day the mediator says a deal is close means the market is pricing scepticism, so gap risk is asymmetric to the downside on any concrete announcement — and a reopening would hit the oil sleeve AND the safe-haven bid under silver at the same time.

topNews.headline: $58bn 3-year auction clears 4.291% with 2.71 cover — but today's $42bn 10-year prices AFTER CPI
topNews.actionable: Strong front-end demand at a higher clearing yield is the most plausible reason the long end held rather than extended. The sequencing is the risk: a hot print forces dealers to underwrite $42bn into a selloff, which is what would push the 30Y through 5.254% and mark down the S-REIT sleeve.

signals: Silver rejected at a seven-week high, oil up 5% in two sessions, positioning long into an inflation print — that configuration cuts both ways tonight. A hot number feeds the inflation impulse that lifts silver AND revives the hike that hurts it, and at 1.6x the second effect compounds against a margin base.

The metals failure is the week's most important tell so far. Gold and silver had oil +1.4%, a 2007-high long end and a fresh Chinese central-bank accumulation story, and still closed red off multi-week highs. Watch whether tonight's print produces a higher HIGH or just another failed one.

GDX beat gold by 10-15bp on a down day. That is not confirmation, because both fell — but the two-session relative-strength deterioration stopped. A gold rally on CPI is the clean test of whether the lag ever meant anything.

Inside the Singapore sleeve the barbell is tilting: banks and developers participated in the reopen (OCBC to a record, UOL +1.22%), the trusts you hold did not move at all. If the 0.00% prints survive a broker check, that divergence is name-specific and worth a direct look at Keppel REIT and the Mapletrees.

Xiaomi at -3.5% underperformed HS Tech's -1.9% and SMIC closed near its session low after a 2-point range — selling into the close rather than stabilisation. Tencent's numbers land after today's HK close, so the sleeve's reaction is a Thursday event, not a today event.
Stacked event risk today: Tencent around the 16:00 HKT close and US CPI at 20:30 SGT, in the same window. A hedge sized for one is exposed to the other.
